text.p: Marriott International Inc. reported better than 20 percent profit increases for its fourth quarter and full year Thursday and said it would introduce a new type of extended-stay lodging for global business executives.

Marriott, which calls itself the world's leading hospitality company, said its net income for the three months ended Jan. 3 grew by 22 percent to $110 million, or 80 cents a share, from $90 million, or 68 cents a share.
For the full year the Washington-based company said net income rose by 24 percent to $306 million, or $2.24 a share, from $247 million, or $1.87 a share.
Marriott said revenues for the quarter expanded by 13 percent to $3.4 billion from $2.9 billion while full-year revenues grew 10 percent to $10.17 billion from $8.96 billion.

"This was an outstanding year for our lodging operations and all of our brands posted excellent results due to a combination of high occupancy levels, substantial room rate growth and expanded distribution," Chairman J.W. Marriott Jr. said in a statement.
The company said its results were helped by contributions from new properties and higher earnings from Marriott's 49 percent interest in the Ritz-Carlton hotel management company.

Marriott said that during the year it added a record 148 properties totalling 18,600 rooms and timeshare villas to its lodging portfolio, which now comprises 1,184 properties totalling 227,000 hotel rooms and 2,900 timeshare villas.
It said that it planned to add at least 120,000 hotel rooms across its lodging brands over the next five years.
Part of the expansion will come from a new hotel brand, Marriott Executive Residences, designed for business executives who plan to stay in an urban destination for 30 days or more.

It said these new hotels -- targeted for emerging markets in the Pacific Rim and Eastern Europe as well as major cities in developed nations -- will offer residential apartments with hotel-like amenities, full kitchens, security and the availability of short-term leases.
Mariott also announced that William J. Shaw, a 22-year veteran of the company, would assume the new position of president and chief operating officer. Shaw, 51, will take up the post March 31.
J.W. Marriott will remain chairman and chief executive officer, the company said.
Marriott International's stock added 75 cents to $54.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
